Shooting marbles (in Northeast China we call it liúliu). As a kid, nobody within a few hundred meters dared play against me, and my matches often drew a crowd of onlookers who clicked their tongues in amazement: what a shot this kid has! The rules: you hold the marble between the knuckle of your thumb and your index finger, curl your other three fingers over your thumb, aim at someone else’s marble on the ground, and flick your thumb to launch your own. Hit their marble and you win it.

Back then I even made a few yuan selling the marbles I’d won. But these days most housing estates are paved with concrete, and with all the electronic gadgets around, the game has all but vanished even in my hometown. I’m not sure kids today have even heard of it.
